generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and sport science, succeeding on your own terms runs across your whole degree, not just the final assessment. You direct a coaching placement or a lab project, notice the practical skill and professional contacts it builds, and keep asking what success in the field means to you. Those small rounds let you say, with evidence, what you have become.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport science finalists reach the same point with similar marks. One banks the grade and waits for graduation. The other directs his placement, notices the coaching skills and industry contacts he has built, and keeps defining what success means to him. By graduation he can show, with evidence, the practitioner he has become, and the first student cannot.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and sport science, succeeding works best as one practice you own. You run all three strands together across the degree: direct your work, build your capital, and define and articulate your success as a practitioner. It is the practice, not any single result, that shows what you have become.

check.body: A final-year student directs her own revision, notices the resilience and networks she has built, and can say with evidence what she set out to achieve. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That she is succeeding as one practice: the engine, her graduate capital and her own definition of success are working together.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three strands are running at once, which is what succeeding on your own terms looks like.

_items.text: That she has a high final grade and nothing more needs saying.
_items.feedback: A grade alone is not the point. She is drawing on all three strands, not just her marks.

_items.text: That she has finished the engine strand and can now drop it.
_items.feedback: Directing your own learning does not stop. The engine keeps running as you become a graduate.

_items.text: That graduate capital is the only strand that matters in the end.
_items.feedback: Capital is one strand. Here it works alongside the engine and her own definition of success.
